solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Knee-jerk reactions feel right, in short, when involved with sex

indicators.note: something put in short form is cut down to its abbreviation, a single letter here, before the mix begins
things that are involved are tangled together, so the letters get jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone trusts their gut instincts when sex enters the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' just shrinks right to R; the anagram signal is 'involved', and FEEL, R and SEX are shuffled together into REFLEXES.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-jerk reaction is the classic automatic response doctors test with a hammer, the textbook example of a reflex.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing American swine crushes left

indicators.note: to crush something is to squeeze it tight in your grip, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: SOB, son of a bitch, is American slang for a swine of a person
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A lazy American pig squashes something left lying around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine' is not a pig here but an insult, and the American insult of choice is SOB; L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a lazy, untidy person, and calling someone a good-for-nothing is the same insult about idleness.

clue.text: Narcissist's erection controlled with elastic and string finally

definitions.note: a possessive noun standing for an adjective: what belongs to a narcissist is self-centred

indicators.note: something elastic stretches and changes shape, so the letters are pulled into a new order
finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
C (Latin cum) is the medical shorthand for with
the last letter of string

explanation.surface: A vain man's arousal is kept in check by elastic and some string.
explanation.walkthrough: The C for 'with' comes from prescriptions, where a c with a bar over it means 'with'. ERECTION plus C and G is mixed by 'elastic'; 'controlled' only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus fell in love with his own reflection, so anything belonging to a narcissist is self-absorbed and self-centred.

clue.text: A sort of sex examination

blocks.note: first meaning: sex using the mouth
second meaning: a spoken test, as in a language exam

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, a kind of medical check on someone's sex life; it is two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names a kind of sexual act, and as a noun it is a spoken test such as a viva or language exam.

clue.text: Handy cash secures 'incorruptible' left-wing leaders with no difficulty

indicators.note: the leaders of words are the letters at their fronts, so each word gives its first letter
to secure something is to lock it safely away, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: the ready, or readies, is British slang for cash in hand
the first letters of incorruptible and left-wing

explanation.surface: A bribe easily buys off left-wing leaders who claim to be incorruptible.
explanation.walkthrough: The ready is British slang for money, especially cash on hand; I and L go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something readily means doing it easily and without hesitation, an adverb synonym for without effort.

clue.text: Tiring day screwing big shot

indicators.note: screwing twists things round, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exhausting day spent in bed with an important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwing' has the obvious bedroom sense in the surface, but it works as a twisting of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dignitary is a person of high rank or office, and big shot is the informal term for such an important figure.

clue.text: Go on the attack when miserable arses pocket two grand

indicators.note: something miserable is in a wretched state, so the letters are knocked out of shape
to pocket something is to tuck it away inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: taken as written
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds, so two of them give GG

explanation.surface: Gloomy idiots get violent once they have pocketed two thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is a thousand pounds, abbreviated G. ARSES is rearranged to ARESS and GG slips in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggress is the rare verb for launching an attack or acting with hostility, the root of aggression and aggressor.

clue.text: Drugs tipped onto spirit which is injected to give immunity

definitions.text: which is injected to give immunity

indicators.note: something tipped up is turned over, and in a down answer that runs its letters upwards

blocks.note: E is ecstasy, so drugs in the plural are Es
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Pills dropped into a glass of spirits make a dangerous cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'tipped' turns the drugs upside down, and 'onto' places them above the spirit, which means first.
explanation.definitionFit: Serum taken from immune blood carries antibodies, so injecting it gives a patient protection against disease.

clue.text: Putting sex back into political party is a silly thing to get up to

definitions.text: a silly thing to get up to

indicators.note: putting something back turns it the other way, so the letters run in reverse
putting one thing into another places it inside

blocks.note: the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party
IT is a crossword stand-in for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A politician declares that reviving a party's sex scandals is just playing the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex is a crossword staple; turned round it sits inside ANC.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a piece of foolish or playful behaviour, the kind of caper or prank people get up to.

clue.text: Whip: "F*** the record!"

blocks.note: the asterisks leave only the first letter of the swear word standing
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A party whip swears at the voting record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests the parliamentary whip, but it is the verb; the starred word just gives F.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip and to flog are both to beat someone with a lash or cane as punishment, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Awful Boris clan protects upper class – they'll need to be focussed

indicators.note: something awful is a terrible mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder
to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the old label for upper-class usage in Britain

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson's dreadful family closes ranks around their posh friends.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' debate on posh British speech; it sits inside the anagram of BORIS CLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Field glasses must be adjusted with a wheel until the image is sharp, so the plural pronoun fits the pair of lenses.

clue.text: (& 14dn.) Organisation prepared to demonstrate it's no longer being associated with a revolting activity

blocks.note: the state of a species that no longer exists at all
revolting here means rising in revolt, not disgusting

explanation.surface: A protest group declares it has cut ties with something disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting but means staging a revolt. Extinction Rebellion is the British-born climate protest movement known for mass street demonstrations.
explanation.definitionFit: The climate campaign group is famous for direct action and street protest, so it is literally an organisation ready to demonstrate.

clue.text: Is a char putting on blubber, winning all prizes?

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British cleaning lady, and what she does is clean
to blubber is to cry noisily

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady piles on weight while sweeping the board at a prize-giving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' looks like fat after 'putting on', but it is the verb meaning to sob; 'putting on' just adds it after the cleaning. A char is an old British word for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean sweep is the idiom for taking every trophy or seat on offer, leaving rivals with nothing.

clue.text: Boris, with sod all right, needs flipping sex frolic?

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: Boris Johnson was Prime Minister, PM for short
sod all is crude British slang for nothing, and nothing is O
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Boris, with nothing going right, has to have a bloody fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word, but it turns PM, O and R round. Sod all is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabloids call a casual sexual encounter a romp, so it is newspaper slang for a playful bout of sex.

clue.text: see 12ac.
One who keeps going round hospital – not Beardie's thing

indicators.note: going round something means circling it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a saver is someone who keeps money back
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient who keeps visiting hospital isn't the bearded type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps going round' looks like one phrase, but it splits: SAVER is the keeper and 'going round' wraps it around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A man with a beard has no use for an electric razor, so the appliance is the very opposite of a bearded man's gadget.

clue.text: Reversal of ban, with US spies going round about an area of north Africa

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective or language of that area, not a place name

indicators.note: a reversal turns something backwards, so the letters run the other way
turning about means facing the opposite way, so the letters read backwards
going round something means encircling it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to bar is to ban
the CIA is America's foreign intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A ban is overturned while American agents hover around a North African region.
explanation.walkthrough: Both abbreviations and synonyms here get turned round, so two reversal signals appear; the second turned piece then wraps around the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the language and culture of the Maghreb and the rest of North Africa, so it describes things from that region.

clue.text: Dawn, Dick, Charles, initially and Barney

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: both are slang for the penis
the first letter of Charles
a barney is British slang for a noisy quarrel or row

explanation.surface: A list of first names, like a roll call of four old friends.
explanation.walkthrough: All four look like people's names; only Dawn is the definition, and the others are a slang word, an initial and a British word for an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosters traditionally crow at first light, so the time of the cockerel's call is a poetic word for daybreak.

clue.text: 'Up yours!' – PO should quit the practice of high interest lending

definitions.text: the practice of high interest lending

indicators.note: to quit is to leave, so those letters walk out of the phrase
things that are up in the air are disturbed, so the remaining letters are stirred about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these two letters go

explanation.surface: A Post Office manager tells the payday lenders exactly where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P and O out of UP YOURS to leave U, Y, U, R, S, then rearrange them. PO is also the Post Office, which is part of the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at an excessive or illegal rate of interest, long condemned by churches and moralists.

clue.text: Boris, a year inside – bloody hell!

indicators.note: something inside is held within other words, so the letters sit across the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Boris, then a and the start of year

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to learn Boris got a year in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A year inside' reads as a prison term, but 'inside' just means the answer sits within the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or shock, the posh British one rather milder than the swearing it stands for.

clue.text: Uncomplaining sort of drunken sot in charge

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: a sot is a drunkard
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A boss who drinks too much never moans about anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like a hedge, but 'sort' belongs to the definition and 'of' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic bears pain and hardship without complaint, after the Greek philosophers who taught calm endurance.

clue.text: Chuck consul out then Conservative leader out? Unfortunately not

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter of the word is used
out means gone, so that letter is removed from the mix
chucking things about throws them into disorder, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Conservative

explanation.surface: A hopeful wish to sack a diplomat and then the Tory leader too, sadly dashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' is both a word in the fodder and the signal to scramble it; one C is removed from CHUCK CONSUL before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a rueful reply meaning the hoped-for thing did not happen, the same as a regretful no.

clue.text: Romantic's sword throw on getting pissed

indicators.note: someone getting drunk loses control, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dashing lover hurls his sword after a few too many drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic' suggests a lover, but here it is the literary movement; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was a leading English poet of the Romantic movement, famous for the daffodils poem.

clue.text: Party officer is a plonker

blocks.note: a do is an informal party
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A political party official is called an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party officer' reads as one official, but it splits into two pieces. Plonker is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are insults for a stupid person; plonker is the British slang term and dolt the older standard one.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Henry briefly following creep, Nick

blocks.note: Hal is a short form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to creep forward slowly

explanation.surface: A man called Henry trails behind a creepy character named Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-inch is Cockney rhyming slang: half-inch rhymes with pinch, which means steal. 'Briefly' shortens Henry to HAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and Cockney rhyming slang uses half-inch for pinch, another word for steal.

clue.text: see 24dn.
Handed over by hospital aid for the purpose of operational cuts?

definitions.text: Handed over by hospital aid for the purpose of operational cuts?

blocks.clueFragment: Handed over by hospital aid for the purpose of operational cuts?
blocks.note: surface reading: money given by a health charity to fund cutbacks in operations
setter's reading: the tool a theatre nurse passes to a surgeon to make incisions during an operation

explanation.surface: Charity funding for a hospital is spent on making cuts to its services.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about budget cuts in the health service; the cuts are really surgical incisions, and the thing handed over is a tool, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small sharp knife is passed over by a nurse in the operating theatre to make incisions.

clue.text: Ex-president's "Fraud!" – holding back nothing by end of count

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters read in reverse
the end of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept
to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: nil means nothing
the last letter of count
a con is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: A former president cries fraud while refusing to concede at the end of a vote count.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes a recent ex-president disputing an election; the answer is a different one. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton served as the 42nd President of the United States in the 1990s, so he is a former holder of that office.
